The full suite is green (7 tests, 0 failures/errors, BUILD SUCCESS).

## Summary

I implemented the rule "reject creating an owner whose normalized telephone is already used by any other owner → 409" by following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions.

**New step in the `POST /api/owners` pipeline** — `CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique`, wired between `normalize` and `build` in `owners.POST.yml`. It runs after telephone normalization, so it compares the canonical ten-digit value against every existing owner's telephone (each reduced to digits the same way, so differently-formatted spellings of the same number still collide). On a match it throws a checked `DuplicateTelephoneException`.

**Escalation handling** — `DuplicateTelephoneException` (checked) plus `DuplicateTelephoneHandler`, which returns a `409 Conflict` `ProblemDetail` naming `telephone` in the `errors` array, mirroring the existing `InvalidTelephone`/`MissingOwnerFields` handlers. ## Summary

I implemented the rule "reject creating an owner whose normalized telephone is already used by any other owner → 409" by following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions.

**New step in the `POST /api/owners` pipeline** — `CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique`, wired between `normalize` and `build` in `owners.POST.yml`. It runs after telephone normalization, so it compares the canonical ten-digit value against every existing owner's telephone (each reduced to digits the same way, so differently-formatted spellings of the same number still collide). On a match it throws a checked `DuplicateTelephoneException`.

**Escalation handling** — `DuplicateTelephoneException` (checked) plus `DuplicateTelephoneHandler`, which returns a `409 Conflict` `ProblemDetail` naming `telephone` in the `errors` array, mirroring the existing `InvalidTelephone`/`MissingOwnerFields` handlers.
